reason: 35 shipped Chinese translations corrected. Reviewed by eight readers over all 816 sentences merged this session, then every proposed replacement was put to an adversary whose default was to refuse — 70 proposed, 35 upheld.

entries.from: 乘公交车时出示了定期票。
entries.to: 乘公交车时出示定期票。
entries.why: The Japanese is habitual (乗るとき…見せます, "whenever I get on the bus"), but the Chinese has the perfective 了, turning it into a one-time past event. Also 定期票 is a Japanism; the Mandarin word for a commuter pass is 月票.

entries.from: 请把浴室的水放掉。
entries.to: 请把浴缸里的水放掉。
entries.why: お風呂の水 is the water in the bathtub (English: "the bathwater"), but 浴室的水 means the water of the bathroom in general — wrong referent.

entries.from: 为了省去麻烦，我使用了新软件。
entries.to: 为了省去麻烦，我使用新软件。
entries.why: The Japanese 使う is non-past/habitual (the software is used in order to save effort), but 使用了 makes it a completed past action.

entries.from: 附近的狗在深夜激烈地吠叫。
entries.to: 附近的狗在深夜狂吠。
entries.why: 激烈地吠叫 is not idiomatic Mandarin — 激烈 is used of fighting or debate, not of a dog barking; Chinese says 狂吠 or 叫得很凶.

entries.from: 昨天的比赛是我们队的败局。
entries.to: 昨天的比赛，球队输了。
entries.why: 败局 means a losing situation still in progress, not a match result; and 我们队 adds a first-person team the Japanese (チームの負け) does not have.

entries.from: 我买了点心作为旅行的特产。
entries.to: 我买了点心作为旅行的伴手礼。
entries.why: 作为旅行的特产 is unidiomatic — 特产 is a region's local produce, not a gift brought back; お土産 here is the souvenir gift itself.

entries.from: 雨过不久就会停吧。
entries.to: 雨不久就会停了吧。
entries.why: 雨过不久就会停吧 misparses: 雨过 reads as "after the rain", garbling the sentence. The subject needs to be separated from 不久.

entries.from: 我站起身来在电车上让座。
entries.to: 我在电车上为了让座站了起来。
entries.why: Word order is broken Mandarin: the locative 在电车上 sits after the verb, so 我站起身来在电车上让座 reads as a garbled chain. The Japanese is 席を譲るために立ち上がった — stood up in order to give up the seat.

entries.from: 我想掌握作为社会人的基本常识。
entries.to: 我想掌握作为职场人应有的基本常识。
entries.why: 社会人 is copied straight from Japanese. In Chinese 社会人 is not the neutral 'working adult' — it reads as slang for a streetwise/gangster type, so the sentence misfires.

entries.from: 小鸟在树上造了一个巢。
entries.to: 一只小鸟正在树上筑巢。
entries.why: Aspect mismatch: 巣を作っている (and the English 'is making a nest') is ongoing, but 造了一个巢 states a completed action.

entries.from: 孩子们沉迷于玩游戏。
entries.to: 孩子们玩游戏玩得入迷。
entries.why: 夢中になっている is neutral absorption, but 沉迷 in Chinese is clearly negative (addiction/losing oneself in something harmful). The Japanese and English ('absorbed in') carry no criticism.

entries.from: 老奶奶给我讲了从前的故事。
entries.to: 奶奶给我讲了从前的故事。
entries.why: おばあさん here (and the English 'my grandmother') is the speaker's own grandmother; 老奶奶 means an unrelated elderly woman.

entries.from: 那位年轻演员在电视剧中聚集了很高的人气。
entries.to: 那位年轻演员在电视剧中人气越来越高。
entries.why: 聚集人气 is not idiomatic Mandarin for 人気を集めている, and 聚集了很高的人气 is a broken collocation (聚集 does not take 高). Aspect is also ongoing in the Japanese.

entries.from: 一只黑猫突然横穿过我的眼前。
entries.to: 一只黑猫突然从我眼前横穿过去。
entries.why: 横穿过我的眼前 is unidiomatic; 横穿 takes the crossed space as object and needs 从…眼前.

entries.from: 我读了一本关于日本历史的书。
entries.to: 我读关于日本历史的书。
entries.why: 日文「読む」是辞书形（习惯/一般动作），中文加了「了」变成已完成的过去事件，体貌不符。

entries.from: 新成员加入了团队。
entries.to: 新成员加入团队。
entries.why: 日文「加わる」是非过去形（英文也是一般现在时 joins），中文的「加入了」变成了已完成事件。

entries.from: 弟弟现在正沉迷于游戏。
entries.to: 弟弟现在正热衷于打游戏。
entries.why: 沉迷 is clearly negative (addiction, wasting oneself), while 熱中 / "absorbed in" is neutral. The Chinese turns a neutral statement about a hobby into a criticism.

entries.from: 学者们主张着不同的学说。
entries.to: 学者们主张不同的学说。
entries.why: 「主张着」is ungrammatical aspect marking; 主张 does not take 着. Also 学者によって異なる説 means different scholars hold different theories.

entries.from: 她作为团队的核心活跃着。
entries.to: 她作为团队的核心十分活跃。
entries.why: 「活跃着」marks an ongoing state, while 活躍した is completed past narration.

entries.from: 我用粗绳子系紧了大包裹。
entries.to: 我用粗绳子捆住了大包裹。
entries.why: 系紧 ("fasten tightly") is the wrong verb for roping up a package — Chinese uses 捆 — and it adds a "tightly" the Japanese 縛りました does not have.

entries.from: 温暖的阳光照进了房间。
entries.to: 温暖的阳光照进房间里来。
entries.why: 入ってきます describes sunlight streaming in now/habitually, but 照进了 marks a completed past event.

entries.from: 下个假期是周六和周日。
entries.to: 下次休息是周六和周日。
entries.why: 休み here means days off (a weekend), while 假期 means a holiday/vacation period.

entries.from: 非但没挨骂，反而收到了表扬。
entries.to: 非但没挨骂，反而受到了表扬。
entries.why: Wrong collocation: 表扬 takes 受到, not 收到 (收到 is for things one receives physically, e.g. mail). 「收到了表扬」is not correct Mandarin.

entries.from: 确认倒垃圾的星期。
entries.to: 确认倒垃圾是星期几。
entries.why: 「确认倒垃圾的星期」is not idiomatic Mandarin — 星期 cannot stand as a bare noun object here. The natural way to say 曜日を確認する is 是星期几.

entries.from: 半夜腹部突然疼痛醒了过来。
entries.to: 半夜肚子突然疼起来，我就醒了。
entries.why: Run-on with a broken verb chain: 「突然疼痛醒了过来」has no connective, and 腹部 is clinical for 夜中にお腹が痛くなる. Reads as ungrammatical.

entries.from: 用坚固的铁链栓住了狗。
entries.to: 用坚固的铁链拴住了狗。
entries.why: Wrong character: 栓 (a bolt/plug, noun) is used where the verb 拴 (to tie/tether) is required. 犬を鎖でつないだ = tied the dog with a chain.

entries.from: 收到了一封来自老家母亲寄来的包裹。
entries.to: 收到了老家母亲寄来的包裹。
entries.why: Wrong classifier: 一封 is for letters, not parcels (包裹). Also 来自…寄来的 is redundant, doubling the source marker.

entries.from: 针对他的意见提出提问。
entries.to: 针对他的意见提出问题。
entries.why: 提出提问 is not a valid collocation (verb+verb); Chinese takes 提问 alone or 提出问题.

entries.from: 每个月都如实缴纳税款。
entries.to: 每个月都认真缴纳税款。
entries.why: 如实 means 'truthfully/as declared' and shifts the sentence to honest tax reporting; しっかり払っている just means paying properly and without fail.

entries.from: 在动物园看见了大象。
entries.to: 在动物园看见了一头很大的大象。
entries.why: 大象 simply means 'elephant', so the 大きな ('big') of the Japanese is dropped — the sentence no longer says the elephant was large.

entries.from: 我摔倒了，折断了脚骨。
entries.to: 我摔倒了，摔断了腿骨。
entries.why: 足 here is the leg (the English says "a bone in my leg"), but Chinese 脚骨 means the bones of the foot; 折断了脚骨 is also unidiomatic for an accidental break.

entries.from: 暑假期间打算去进行长期出国旅行。
entries.to: 暑假期间要去海外长期旅行。
entries.why: 「去进行长期出国旅行」 is unidiomatic — 去 plus 进行 is redundant, and 出国旅行 as the object of 进行 does not collocate.

entries.from: 周日的车站人山人海，可真不容易。
entries.to: 周日的车站人山人海，真是够受的。
entries.why: 大変でした means it was exhausting/rough; 「可真不容易」 shifts this to "it wasn't easy (to accomplish)", a different sense.

entries.from: 我发呆地望着窗外。
entries.to: 我呆呆地望着窗外。
entries.why: 发呆 is a verb phrase and cannot take 地 as a manner adverbial; 「发呆地望着」 is ungrammatical.

entries.from: 独自举起重箱子。
entries.to: 独自举起很重的箱子。
entries.why: 「重箱子」 is not idiomatic Mandarin — a monosyllabic 重 cannot directly modify 箱子 this way.
